opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write unless their role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is not permitted. Granting write as the maximum allowed.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E039 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training are limited to read on any system (never admin). Admin request exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: Belinda Fuentes (E039) requested admin to Payroll. The two agents' notes conflict on the decisive fact: HR reports full_time Analyst (max write, since Analyst does not own Payroll), while Security reports contractor with basic training (max read; never admin). Under both interpretations admin is above the maximum. Given the unresolved conflict on employment type, I apply the least-privilege maximum (read) so that access does not violate the stricter, security-based constraint. Grant read.

- Security says: employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read

This is a conflict between HR and Security databases. As the Approver, I need to make the final decision.

Key considerations:
- Access policy: full_time employees can have up to write, admin only if their role owns the system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist does). So HR says max write.
- Contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Security says contractor with basic training → max read.

There's a conflict on employment type: HR says full_time, Security says contractor. Both claim to have looked it up in their own database.

As the Approver, I have to decide. Typically, in these scenarios, the tie-breaker might be the security agent's recommendation being more conservative, or we might need to weigh which is more reliable.

The requested level is admin. Regardless of which note we believe, admin is not permitted:
- If full_time Analyst: max is write (HR says grant write as maximum)
- If contractor with basic training: max is read (Security says grant read)
